A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MEGA-GNN, retaining the two-stage multigraph aggregation framework and overlapping AML/ETH experiments. The complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial renaming and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original AML edge-classification and ETH node-classification experiments, component and port-number ablations, and inference-throughput measurements, including supplementary results in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 reports original financial and social-network experiments, synthetic node regression, controlled ablations, and runtime/memory measurements in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The central two-stage, bidirectional architecture remains. v3 adds MEGA-RGCNE, combining PNA-style first-stage pooling with relation-specific transformations in the second stage (Appendix C.5). It also revises the written reverse-edge update to include the previous individual edge embedding, unlike v1 Equation 10 (v3 Equation 11). These are limited procedural extensions; the neighbor-aware terminology itself does not establish a new method.

E1.justification: Beyond v1's AML transaction classification and ETH phishing detection, v3 evaluates Reddit, Wikipedia and MOOC user-state prediction and a synthetic per-neighbor-statistics regression task. It also includes AML Large HI/LI and ETH scenarios with artificially collapsed parallel edges. The added social domain, regression task and altered graph-input conditions substantially broaden coverage.

E2.justification: AML comparisons add plain GenAgg, R-GCNE, FraudGT, Multi-FraudGT and an edge-classification adaptation of DIAM (v3 Tables 16 and 20). ETH adds DIAM and Multi-FraudGT while dropping the reported ADAMM-GenAgg and Multi-GenAgg rows. JODIE participates in the new social-network comparison. GFP+LightGBM and GFP+XGBoost remain in Appendix E.1 rather than being removed.

E3.justification: New protocols include independently generated synthetic train/validation/test graphs evaluated by MAE, 60/20/20 temporal social splits evaluated by ROC-AUC, capacity-matched controls and neighborhood-size sweeps. AML PR-AUC reporting disappears. ETH splitting changes in the description from transactions in v1 Section 4 to nodes ordered by first transaction in v3 Appendix C.4, retaining 65/15/20 proportions. This is a reported protocol revision; unchanged overlapping scores do not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds synthetic aggregation diagnostics, ETH edge-collapse tests, AML random-grouping controls, capacity-matched comparisons, and empirical sampling-size, memory and training-cost analyses. Existing component ablations gain base-model comparisons and medium AML datasets but lose the ego-ID-only configurations. The port-permutation study is revised from Multi-GIN/Multi-PNA to Multi-PNA/Multi-FraudGT. These substantially expand tests of mechanism, confounding and scalability beyond v1.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations across different seeds: five runs in v1 and at least five in v3, without establishing an increase for retained experiments. v3 adds a focused set of two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests across six paired AML dataset scores (Appendix E.4, Table 21). The comparison against the strongest non-MEGA baseline yields p=0.093.

E6.justification: Retained AML entries change between v1 Table 2 and v3 Table 16: MEGA-GIN Medium LI F1 changes from 39.03 to 46.05, and MEGA-GenAgg Small HI from 74.88 to 74.48. Multi-FraudGT now leads Small HI at 75.81. Extensive new task, control and resource results appear, while mixed-aggregator AML rows, GenAgg-based ETH rows and PR-AUC results disappear. These are reported result revisions, not established same-setting algorithmic gains.

T1.justification: v1's conditional-universality theorem, unique-node-ID lemma and BFS proof construction are removed. v3 introduces formal single-stage and neighbor-aware operators and a new expressiveness theorem for sum/raw-moment aggregators, whose proof assumes a constant edge-feature coordinate. Its complexity analysis includes linear transformations and node activations, extending v1's aggregation-focused analysis. The permutation-equivariance proof and port-number proposition/counterexample are also revised.

C1.justification: v1 foregrounds artificial nodes, universality under strict edge ordering and financial-task performance. v3 drops MEGA-GNN's universality contribution and foregrounds the neighbor-aware operator, stronger moment-based expressiveness and equal asymptotic complexity. Principal empirical claims extend to social networks. AML superiority is qualified through 17-of-18 comparisons against corresponding Multi-GNN variants and MEGA-PNA leading five of six datasets against all reported competitors.

C2.justification: v3 attributes gains more specifically to correct neighbor grouping and the concentration of illicit transactions on multi-edge pairs, and addresses parameter-count and efficiency explanations. Limitations now identify the moment-based theoretical scope and untested application domains, replacing v1's emphasis on evolving multigraphs. Appendix F also replaces v1's categorical dismissal of fairness concerns with substantive discussion of false positives, inherited bias, interpretability and human oversight.

D1.justification: v3 supplies a repository URL and states that code, preprocessing, training scripts and configurations are public, replacing v1's future-release promise. It adds software/CUDA versions, CPU/RAM specifications, timing boundaries, parameter counts, dataset statistics, temporal graph-construction details and R-GCNE settings (Appendices C–D). The original GIN/PNA hyperparameters and two-hop, 100-neighbor sampling remain largely unchanged; these disclosures do not imply wholesale experimental reconfiguration.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially to DIAM, FraudGT, JODIE, relational architectures and their expressiveness, aggregation theory, and financial-crime applications. Appendix A develops the distinction and complementarity between relation-aware and neighbor-aware processing. Earlier universality/random-initialization and subgraph-method discussions are reduced. This changes the research positioning beyond bibliographic updates or moving the related-work section.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and method exposition are extensively rewritten around neighbor-aware aggregation. Related work moves from Section 5 to Section 2, while detailed limitations of existing methods move to Appendix A. Experiments are reorganized into diagnostic, social, financial, ablation and scalability sections, and the appendices are restructured. The title, authorship listing and publication header also change.

P2.justification: v3 redraws the aggregation illustration and introduces detailed layer diagrams and relational-model diagrams. The AML presentation shifts from v1's colored result table to main-text comparison plots with expanded appendix tables. ETH results are reformatted, component tables gain parameter counts, and new control/resource tables and scalability plots appear. Existing Multi-GNN/ADAMM illustrations are combined and relocated to the appendix.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the empirical explanation of why the method works. Random-grouping, edge-collapse and capacity-matched controls address important alternatives left unresolved by v1's benchmark and component comparisons. Broader evaluated competitors, social-domain validation, measured resource costs and concrete reproducibility information make the evidence more assessable. Statistical tests and substantive limitations also temper the claims. PR-AUC results are lost, and the changed ETH split description alongside unchanged scores remains unresolved, but these drawbacks do not outweigh the substantial gains in experimental support and transparency.
